yaml_syntax_rules.rule: DATE_TRUNC requires a single-quoted interval string
yaml_syntax_rules.note: The interval keyword MUST be single-quoted inside DATE_TRUNC.

yaml_syntax_rules.rule: TIMESTAMPADD / TIMESTAMPDIFF use bare unquoted singular unit keywords
yaml_syntax_rules.note: Unit is a bare keyword (MONTH, DAY, HOUR, MINUTE, SECOND), singular, no quotes.
Use EXTRACT(unit FROM col), not DATE_PART.

yaml_syntax_rules.rule: Materialization (Public Preview) is an optional top-level block
yaml_syntax_rules.correct:
materialization:
  schedule: every 6 hours
  mode: relaxed
  materialized_views:
    - name: sales_baseline
      type: unaggregated
yaml_syntax_rules.note: mode must be 'relaxed'. materialized_views is a non-empty list; each entry has a unique name and type 'unaggregated' or 'aggregated'. aggregated entries list 'dimensions'/'measures' by their defined names (use the 'dimensions' key even if the view uses 'fields'). schedule is optional (omit for manual refresh only); TRIGGER ON UPDATE is not supported. Do not emit materialization during dry-run validation.

yaml_syntax_rules.rule: DATEDIFF takes exactly two arguments and returns days
yaml_syntax_rules.note: For other units use TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, start, end).

yaml_syntax_rules.rule: All string literals must be single-quoted everywhere in expressions
yaml_syntax_rules.note: Applies to comparisons, CASE THEN/ELSE results, IN lists, CONCAT separators, LIKE patterns.

yaml_syntax_rules.rule: CASE WHEN results that contain special characters must be single-quoted
yaml_syntax_rules.note: Every THEN and ELSE value that is a string literal needs quotes.

yaml_syntax_rules.rule: FILTER clause syntax uses parenthesized WHERE
Join 'on' clause uses source.col = alias.col format
yaml_syntax_rules.note: The root table is always 'source'; joined tables use their 'name' alias. Never use fully qualified names in join on clauses.

yaml_syntax_rules.rule: Dimension/measure expressions referencing joined table columns use alias.col
yaml_syntax_rules.note: Use the short join name (alias), not the fully qualified table name.

yaml_syntax_rules.rule: Version must be string '1.1' not number 1.1
CONCAT separator arguments must be single-quoted string literals
yaml_syntax_rules.note: Any non-column, non-function argument in CONCAT must be a quoted string. -Q is parsed as 'subtract column Q' without quotes.

yaml_syntax_rules.rule: Window measures use a 'window' array with 'order', 'range'/'rows', and 'semiadditive'
yaml_syntax_rules.note: Window is an ARRAY of specs. Use 'order' (not 'order_by'). Range uses 'trailing N day' syntax (not INTERVAL). Include 'semiadditive: first|last'.

measure_patterns.description: Templates for non-trivial measures. Replace placeholders (col, cond, entity_col, etc.) with actual column names from the metadata.

rate.template: SUM(CASE WHEN {condition} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)

examples.name: Fulfillment Rate
examples.expr: SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'fulfilled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)

examples.name: Readmission Rate
examples.expr: SUM(CASE WHEN is_readmission = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)
examples.comment: Fraction of encounters that are readmissions

examples.name: Conversion Rate
examples.expr: SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'converted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)

examples.name: Orders per Account
examples.comment: Average number of orders per account

percentage.template: ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN {condition} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1)

examples.name: Return Pct
examples.expr: ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN is_returned = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1)

examples.name: Overdue Pct
examples.expr: ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN due_date < current_date() AND status != 'paid' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1)

examples.name: Active Customers
examples.expr: COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FILTER (WHERE last_order_date >= DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', current_date()))

examples.name: Repeat Patients
examples.comment: Patients with more than one visit

examples.name: Avg Wait Time
examples.comment: Average minutes from arrival to being seen

window_rolling.template: AVG(SUM({col})) with window: [{order: date_col, range: trailing N day, semiadditive: last}]

examples.name: 7-Day Rolling Order Count
examples.comment: Rolling 7-day average of daily order counts

window_cumulative.template: SUM(SUM({col})) with window: [{order: date_col, range: unbounded, semiadditive: last}]

join_templates.description: Correct join format for Unity Catalog metric views. The root table is always referenced as 'source'; joined tables are referenced by their short 'name' alias.

star_schema.description: Fact table joins one or more dimension tables

example.note: Dimensions from joined tables use alias.column format (e.g. customers.segment). The fact table columns use bare names (e.g. total_amount).

snowflake.description: Nested joins where a dimension table joins another dimension (DBR 17.1+)

common_mistakes: Using fully qualified names in 'on' clause: on: catalog.schema.orders.customer_id = catalog.schema.customers.id -- WRONG
Using 'using' instead of 'on' for non-trivial joins -- 'using' only works for same-named columns
Forgetting to reference joined columns with alias prefix in dimensions/measures
Using the same alias name as a column name in the source table
Emitting a join 'type'/'join_type' key -- metric-view joins have NO such key; they are always LEFT OUTER JOIN by spec

join_semantics.join_type: Metric-view joins are ALWAYS a LEFT OUTER JOIN from the source (fact) to each joined (dimension) table -- there is no join-type key and you must not emit one. Fact rows are preserved even when a dimension row is missing, so a join never drops or reduces the fact grain.
join_semantics.composite_key: For a multi-column join, put the full condition in 'on' ANDed together: on: source.order_id = lines.order_id AND source.line_no = lines.line_no. (Alternatively 'using: [col1, col2]' when the columns are identically named on both sides -- never both 'on' and 'using'.)
join_semantics.cardinality: Each join accepts an optional 'cardinality' key. It defaults to 'many_to_one' (many fact rows -> one dimension row); OMIT it in that normal case. Set 'cardinality: one_to_many' ONLY when the joined table has multiple rows per source row and you intend to aggregate it as a separate fact source. Never set one_to_many just to reach extra columns -- that fans out and inflates the source's own measures.

format_patterns.description: Format specs propagate to AI/BI dashboards and Genie responses. Infer format from measure semantics.

currency.note: Any monetary aggregate. currency_code (ISO-4217) is REQUIRED when type is currency.

percentage.note: Rates and ratios that represent fractions. For expressions that already multiply by 100, use type: number instead.

number.note: Counts, averages, and numeric scores. Default when no other format applies.

guiding_principles: DIMENSIONAL MODEL IS THE FOUNDATION: Metric views are a dimensional-model construct. They work most easily and correctly against a FACT + DIMENSION structure -- a central fact/transactional table (the measures + grain) surrounded by dimension/lookup tables joined by foreign keys -- OR against any table that is SHAPED LIKE that (a wide denormalized/OBT 'one big table' with measure columns plus descriptive attribute columns, a pre-aggregated mart, an event/transaction log). Before generating, decide how the in-scope tables map onto this shape: pick the fact (measures + grain), treat descriptive tables/columns as dimensions. If the data does not resemble fact + dimension at all (e.g. a pure key-value store, a narrow bridge with no measures, unstructured blobs), a metric view is a poor fit -- prefer a single simple aggregate or skip it rather than forcing joins.

GRAIN FIRST, THEME SECOND: Each metric view declares its grain via its source table (one row = one encounter, one order line, one prescription fill). All measures must be valid at that grain. Do NOT mix measures implying different grains in one view. Within a single grain, create separate views for different analytical themes.

STAR + SNOWFLAKE: Star-schema joins are the default (source -> dim). For dimension hierarchies (customer -> nation -> region), use nested joins with the child 'on' referencing the parent alias. Limit nesting to 2 levels.
ANALYTICAL RICHNESS: Every view should have at least one ratio measure, one computed dimension, and one filtered or conditional aggregate. Simple COUNT(*)-only views are insufficient.

SOURCE FROM FACTS, JOIN TO DIMENSIONS: A metric view's source table should be a FACT/transactional table (the grain-defining table with the numeric measures). Dimension tables are reached via joins and used for grouping, not as view sources -- unless a question is purely about a dimension entity (e.g. customer counts by region), in which case a dimension-only view with no joins is correct.

ONE BROAD VIEW PER FACT GRAIN (comprehensive default): Prefer a single rich view per fact grain with all relevant measures and dimensions; the consumer (Genie, agents, SQL) selects what it needs per query. Split into multiple views from the same source ONLY when the persistent filter, join path, or grain genuinely changes -- not merely for different 'themes'.

RESPECT THE CONFIRMED DATA MODEL: When the context names confirmed fact/source tables (from the user's reviewed ERD), source your views from THOSE tables and use the confirmed joins; treat other tables as dimensions to join to, not as additional view sources.
SIMPLE SCHEMAS ARE FINE: When there are no FK relationships or join paths, create single-table metric views with direct aggregations. Do NOT fabricate joins to manufacture richness.

fact_dimension_model.description: Metric views target a fact + dimension (dimensional) model. Classify the in-scope tables against these roles so views are sourced and joined correctly. Mirrors the roles dbxmetagen's ERD recommender assigns; the metadata context may already state a table's role.
fact_dimension_model.fact: Grain-defining transactional table: many numeric measure columns, typically several outbound foreign keys to dimensions, named fct_/fact_/f_ or flagged as a 'primary'/'fact' entity. Metric views are SOURCED from facts.
fact_dimension_model.dimension: Descriptive lookup table: a near-unique low-null natural key, few or no numeric measures, referenced by facts (inbound FKs, no outbound), named dim_/d_ or flagged 'referenced'/'dimension'/'contextual'. Dimensions are JOINED to and used for grouping; never SUM/AVG their numeric columns from a fact-sourced view.
fact_dimension_model.bridge: A table that is both an FK source and destination (appears in a snowflake chain, e.g. store -> region). Reach it via nested joins, not flat siblings.
fact_dimension_model.fact_like_tables: Many real tables are not labeled fact/dim but ARE shaped like a fact and work well as a view source: a wide denormalized / OBT ('one big table') that carries both measure columns and descriptive attribute columns (treat the measures as the fact, the attribute columns as inline dimensions -- no joins needed); a pre-aggregated summary/mart table (direct aggregations, usually no joins); an event or transaction log (one row per event = the grain). Map these onto the fact role rather than skipping them.
fact_dimension_model.poor_fit: If a table is NOT fact-like at all -- a pure key-value/EAV store, a narrow join/bridge table with no measures, a reference code list with nothing to aggregate, or unstructured blob columns -- a metric view adds little value. Prefer a single simple aggregate, fold it in as a dimension of a real fact, or skip it. Do not fabricate a fact grain that the data does not have.
fact_dimension_model.measurable_column: Numeric, low-null, and NOT a near-unique key. IDs and codes are dimensions/keys, not measures, even when numeric.
fact_dimension_model.grain_column: The unique, low-null natural key that defines one row of the table -- used for COUNT(DISTINCT ...) denominators and to reason about grain.

anti_patterns: NEVER produce a metric view whose only measure is COUNT(*) or COUNT(1). Always add at least one ratio, rate, or filtered aggregate.
NEVER mix measures implying different grains in the same view (e.g. patient-level counts + encounter-level rates from an encounters-sourced view).
NEVER use unquoted string literals in any SQL expression. Every string value must be single-quoted.
NEVER invent column names. Only reference columns that exist in the metadata context provided.
NEVER create duplicate metric views for the same analytical theme. Consolidate related measures into one view.
NEVER use plural date units (MONTHS, HOURS) or quoted units in TIMESTAMPADD/TIMESTAMPDIFF.
NEVER omit joins when FK relationships exist and the questions ask for breakdowns by attributes in another table.
NEVER use bare column names in joined table references. Always qualify with the join alias (customers.segment, not segment when it comes from a joined table).
NEVER prefix dimension names with the join alias in the display name. Use 'Industry' not 'account.Industry'.
NEVER use DATE_PART -- use EXTRACT(unit FROM col) instead.
NEVER return a metric view with zero dimensions or zero measures.

ALL string literals in expr fields MUST be single-quoted, including multi-word values and values with parentheses. Examples: source.State = 'Active', source.Risk IN ('1 - High', '2 - Medium'), THEN 'Mild (Grade 1)', THEN 'Serious (Grade 3+)', status IN ('Related', 'Possibly Related').

NEVER use SQL window functions (OVER, PARTITION BY, ROW_NUMBER, LAG, LEAD) in measure expressions. Metric views do not support window functions in SQL. For rolling/trailing calculations, use the 'window' property on the measure definition instead.
NEVER place chained joins as flat siblings (e.g. customer and nation both at root level with nation.on referencing customer). Use nested joins instead.

NEVER aggregate dimension-table numeric columns (SUM, AVG) from a fact-sourced metric view with joins. SUM(accounts.bed_count) from a prescriptions-sourced view counts bed_count once per prescription, not once per account. Use dimension columns only as grouping dimensions, or create a SEPARATE dimension-only metric view with NO fact-table joins.

NEVER create share-of-total measures like SUM(x)/SUM(x) or SUM(x)/SUM(total). The denominator is grouped identically to the numerator, always producing 1.0. Metric views cannot use OVER() for ungrouped totals. Use conditional aggregates (FILTER) or within-grain rates instead.

NEVER join a fact source to another fact table (tables prefixed fact_/fct_/f_ or with high row counts). Fact-to-fact joins create one-to-many fan-out that inflates ALL aggregates in the view. If you need another fact's columns, create a SEPARATE metric view sourced from that table.

NEVER include a join whose columns you do not actually use in a dimension or measure. Joins 'for completeness' or 'in case they are needed' waste query resources and risk fan-out inflation. Every join must be referenced by at least one dimension/measure expression via its alias.

NEVER reach the same physical dimension table via multiple join paths unless each path is a genuinely different FK role (e.g. ship_to_address vs bill_to_address). If the source already has a direct FK to a dimension, do NOT also reach it through a nested chain.
validation_checklist: All measures are valid at the declared grain of the source table
Every string literal in every expression is single-quoted (comparisons, CASE results, IN lists, LIKE patterns, CONCAT separators)
Every column reference exists in the provided metadata (source table or joined table)
DATE_TRUNC uses quoted interval: DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', col)
TIMESTAMPADD/TIMESTAMPDIFF use bare singular unit: TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, 1, col)
At least one non-trivial measure exists (ratio, rate, filtered aggregate, or conditional count -- not just COUNT(*) and SUM)
Joins are included when FK relationships exist AND questions reference attributes from related tables
Root join 'on' clauses use source.col = alias.col format; nested join 'on' clauses use parent_alias.col = child_alias.col
Dimensions from joined tables use alias.col format in their expr (including nested aliases like nation.name)
Every measure and dimension has a descriptive 'comment' field
Metric view 'name' is unique, reflects grain and analytical theme (not just the table name)
The 'source' field is a fully qualified three-part name (catalog.schema.table)
FILTER clauses use the (WHERE ...) syntax with parentheses
Every measure has a 'format' object: {"type": "currency"}, {"type": "percentage"}, or {"type": "number"}
Every measure and dimension has 'display_name' (human-readable label) and 'synonyms' (array of 2-5 alternative names)

If a 'materialization' block is present: mode is 'relaxed', materialized_views is non-empty, each entry has a unique name and type 'unaggregated'/'aggregated', aggregated entries reference only defined dimensions/measures, and schedule (if set) avoids TRIGGER ON UPDATE
